# Overview

This vignette documents the `mrm_otis_*()`, `mrm_tps_*()`, and
`mrm_siu_*()` empirical callables. Each is a one-line entry point to
one analysis. The OTIS and TPS examples run on the small reference
samples returned by `morie_sample()`; the SIU examples run on the
corpus bundled in rmoriedata. The vignette needs no network access.

For the full datasets:

* OTIS -> `morie_load_dataset("otisb01")` (downloads from
  data.ontario.ca on first call, then reads the local cache)
* TPS -> `morie_fetch_tps("Assault")` (ArcGIS REST)
* SIU -> `morie_fetch_siu()` (the rmoriedata corpus by default; a
  live fetch with `options(morie.siu.allow_fetch = TRUE)`)

See `vignette("mrm-dataset-fetchers")` for the dataset side.

```{r load}
library(rmorie)
b01 <- morie_sample("otis_b01")
b09 <- morie_sample("otis_b09")
tps <- morie_sample("tps_assault")

# Some events carry latitude and longitude 0, i.e. no usable
# location; drop them before any spatial analysis.
sum(tps$LAT_WGS84 == 0 | tps$LONG_WGS84 == 0)
tps <- tps[tps$LAT_WGS84 != 0 & tps$LONG_WGS84 != 0, ]
```

Left in, those points stretch the grid used by
`mrm_tps_moran_clustering()` across the Atlantic, put almost every
Toronto event in one cell, and add steps of thousands of kilometres to
`mrm_tps_levy_scaling()`.

# OTIS suite

## Placement-count concentration on `b09`

The b09 long-format file publishes per (fiscal year x placement-count
band x gender) counts of individuals in segregation. The callable
expands the banded counts using midpoints and returns Hill-MLE Pareto
exponent, Gini coefficient, mean placements per individual, and the
top-k% concentration share.

```{r b09}
mrm_otis_placement_concentration(b09)
```

The values are computed *within fiscal year*: OTIS
`UniqueIndividual_ID` has format `YYYY-XXXXX-SG` and is randomly
reassigned every fiscal year, so cross-year tracking is invalid by
design.

## Segregation-duration KM on `b01`

`NumberConsecutiveDays_Segregation` is the duration in days of each
placement (no censoring -- all durations are observed). The callable
reports per stratum the mean and median duration, `q75_days` (the
75th percentile: the duration that a quarter of placements exceed),
the percentage of placements above the UN Mandela 15-day cutoff, and
the durations at which the empirical survival function falls to 50,
25, 10, 5 and 1 percent.

```{r b01-duration}
mrm_otis_seg_duration_km(b01)
mrm_otis_seg_duration_km(b01, group_cols = "MentalHealth_Alert")
```

This callable replaces the misreading of `YYYY-XXXXX-SG` as a
persistent person identifier, which produces a spurious cross-year
"time-to-readmission" artifact.

## Mortification co-occurrence (alert columns)

The three b01 alert flags (`MentalHealth_Alert`, `SuicideRisk_Alert`,
`SuicideWatch_Alert`) co-occur to a degree well above independence.
The substantive figure is `MentalHealth x SuicideRisk` Cramer's V.

```{r mortification}
mrm_otis_mortification_cooccurrence(b01)
```

## Region locality

`mrm_otis_region_locality()` cross-tabulates the region at the time
of placement against the most recent region. The diagonal share is the
fraction of placements whose region did not change:

```{r region}
res <- mrm_otis_region_locality(b01)
print(res$table)
cat("diagonal share:", res$diagonal_share, "  V:", res$cramers_v, "\n")
```

## Mandela classification

`mrm_classify_mandela()` supports three denominators:

```{r mandela}
mrm_classify_mandela(b01, denominator = "row")           # per-placement
mrm_classify_mandela(b01, denominator = "individual_any") # per-person
mrm_classify_mandela(b01, denominator = "individual_cumulative")
```

The per-individual rates by fiscal year come from table c11, which
`morie_sample("otis_c11")` returns whole.
`morie_otis_analyze_c11_mandela_classification()` classifies the
individuals in each year as at or below 15 days (solitary) or above
(torture, in the function's labels):

```{r c11-mandela}
c11 <- morie_sample("otis_c11")
m11 <- morie_otis_analyze_c11_mandela_classification(c11)
rows <- lapply(m11$tables[[1]]$rows, function(r) unlist(lapply(r, as.character)))
tab11 <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows))
names(tab11) <- m11$tables[[1]]$headers
tab11[tab11$Type == "Segregation", ]
```

# TPS suite

## Levy-flight Hill exponent on inter-event step lengths

Treats consecutive events in chronological order as a single stream
and computes the haversine inter-event step length (km). Returns the
Hill-MLE exponent restricted to steps above `min_step_km`.

```{r tps-levy}
mrm_tps_levy_scaling(tps)
```

## Moran's I + DBSCAN clustering

Grids the WGS84 extent into a coarse raster, counts events per cell,
and computes the global Moran's I via a rook-contiguity matrix. Also
runs DBSCAN on the raw lat/long points (rescaled to km) for cluster
counts.

```{r tps-moran}
mrm_tps_moran_clustering(tps, grid_resolution = 20L)
```

For the full Assault layer, read the file that
`morie_fetch_tps("Assault")` writes (`utils::read.csv()` on the
returned path), drop the zero coordinates, and pass the data frame.

## Neighbourhood inter-event recurrence

For each `HOOD_158` neighbourhood, sorts events chronologically and
computes the gap (in days) between consecutive events.

```{r tps-recur}
head(mrm_tps_neighbourhood_recurrence_km(tps))
```

## Hawkes manifest loader

`mrm_tps_load_hawkes_refit(manifest_path)` reads a
`paper_hawkes_refit.json` manifest of per-category Hawkes fits and
returns it as a data frame. No manifest ships with the package, so
`manifest_path` must point to one you have produced.

# SIU suite

The SIU callables operate on the SIU.csv file that
`morie_fetch_siu()` writes. By default it writes the panel-reviewed
corpus bundled in rmoriedata (English and French reports); `lang = "en"`
keeps the English rows.

```{r siu}
siu_path <- morie_fetch_siu(lang = "en")
siu <- utils::read.csv(siu_path)
dim(siu)
res <- mrm_siu_case_to_decision_km(siu)
print(res$pooled)
head(res$by_service[order(-res$by_service$n), ])
head(mrm_siu_per_service_rate(siu))
```

`mrm_siu_case_to_decision_km()` measures the days from incident to
the Director's decision; open cases are treated as censored. The
`max_days` column shows that some incident dates in the corpus are
decades before the decision, so check extreme rows before using the
mean.
